messages:
Alex Kim: Quick sync 1: we need to finalize the plan for migrating console analytics to the new sharded metrics_index. Thinking dual-write + per-tenant feature flag reads.
Maria Lopez: Whats changed in the storage shape? Need exact field map so console queries can adapt.
Alex Kim: metrics_v1 stores a JSON blob per event. metrics_index stores one row per tenant/hour with precomputed aggregates and tags: (tenant_id, hour_bucket, metric_name, value, tags_hash). Less cardinality in queries.
Jordan Patel: Benefit: UI p95 should drop a lot for heavy dashboards. Risk: missing aggregates during dual-write/backfill, and new shard hotspots.
Sandeep Rao: Ops: plan to shard by tenant_id % 256. That means uneven hot tenants could overload some shards. We should pre-calc tenant write frequency and move a few heavy tenants to dedicated shards.
Priya Nair: From product: users notice inconsistency. If some workspaces see instant charts and others fallback to legacy read, we need a clear banner and consistent sort order.
Alex Kim: Proposed rollout: 1) Ingest dual-write for 72h. 2) Reconciliation + throttled backfill. 3) Read-adapter with feature-flag per tenant (canary 3% -> 10% -> 100%). 4) Circuit-breaker on shard CPU/latency to auto-fall back.
Jordan Patel: Reconciliation query to detect missing hour buckets:
```
SELECT t.tenant_id, h.hour, COUNT(*) as missing
FROM (SELECT tenant_id, generate_series(min_time, max_time, '1 hour') AS hour FROM tenant_time_ranges) t
LEFT JOIN metrics_index m ON m.tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND m.hour_bucket = t.hour
WHERE m.tenant_id IS NULL
GROUP BY t.tenant_id, t.hour
ORDER BY missing DESC
LIMIT 200;
```
Maria Lopez: Run this in shadow first to estimate volume. Backfill should be resumable with per-tenant cursors and S3 resume tokens.
Sandeep Rao: Backfill job constraints: max_rows_per_min, per-shard concurrency, and a global rate cap to protect DB. Use a small thread pool and exponential backoff on conflicts. Log progress to ops topic.
Priya Nair: UX metrics to capture: chart_latency_ms, chart_fallback_rate, banner_impressions, user_acknowledgements. Product wants AB test variants for banner copy.
Alex Kim: Telemetry: emit metric_read.path (index|fallback|v1), metric_read.latency_ms, reconcile.missing_count, backfill.rate. Retain these events for 7d during canary.
Jordan Patel: Quotas: new reads might bypass console cache, so tag reads with quota_label=metrics_index to ensure billing and throttling works. Also update console quota dashboards.
Maria Lopez: Alerting suggestions: 1) reconcile.missing_count > 500/hr sustained, 2) read_adapter_error_rate > 0.5% 5m, 3) shard_cpu_p95 > 80% for 5m.
Sandeep Rao: Router circuit-breaker: if shard_cpu_p95 > 70% OR read_latency_p95 > 600ms, mark tenants on that shard to fallback route. We can use existing router scoreboard to flip quickly.
Priya Nair: Product note: put a toggle to enable/disable banner per workspace. Also show a lighter skeleton instead of full charts when fallback occurs.
Alex Kim: Dev tasks: dual-write impl, reconcile job, throttled backfill worker, read-adapter behind feature-flag, router circuit-breaker.
Jordan Patel: Ill own backfill prototype + SQL heuristics. Will push a PoC to staging by Tue.
Sandeep Rao: Ill own runbook + circuit thresholds. Drafting playbook with rollback steps and commands.
Maria Lopez: Ill run staging canary with 100 test tenants and collect telemetry. Also wiring quota labels.
Priya Nair: Ill prepare banner copy + experiment flags.
Alex Kim: Rollback commands example for ops:
- `rbacctl feature-flag disable use_metrics_index --env=prod`
- `kubectl scale deployment metrics-backfill -n analytics --replicas=0`
- `splunk query: index=analytics metrics_index_errors | stats count by shard`
Alex Kim: Also add a lightweight profiler to log expensive queries against metrics_index; if p95_query_time > 500ms for a shard, trigger auto-fallback.
Maria Lopez: Test matrix: unit tests, staging dual-write 100 tenants, pre-prod 10 tenants 24h, prod canary 3% 24h, expand 10% 48h, expand 100% 7d.
Sandeep Rao: Ill add alerts and an automated playbook. Who approves the dedicated shard list for heavy tenants?
Jordan Patel: Ops+billing to approve. We should identify top 20 tenants by query volume and flag them for dedicated shards during canary.
Priya Nair: UX fallback copy draft: "We're updating metrics for your workspace. Some charts may take longer to load; we're working to restore full performance." Two variants for experiment.
deploy-bot: Deployed read-adapter v2 to staging (build: 2026.03.20-512). Canary tests running.
Alex Kim: Meeting cadence: daily quick-check for the first 72h of canary. Final sync Thu 10:00. Thanks everyone.
